chapter: Orleans Pleasure Club to PWA band
title: Jelly Roll at the Orleans Pleasure Club
summary: Jelly Roll Morton came to the club around 1920 or earlier, brought by Freddie Lucian's father; the club's location and his dislike of parades.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Oh fine, now something you mentioned earlier, what year about would that be when you spoke about, you heard Jelly Roll more?
Oh that's been, that's before I went to the war, that's around 19, 1920, something like that.
Oh yeah, real early. What, you mean the First World War? Yeah. Or before the First World War?

Well yeah, yeah, I didn't go to war until I was 26. I was 26 years old when I came back. But Jelly Roll, you see, they had a fella, he was a, I'm talking about Fred's daddy, he was a good ball player, you see. Freddie Washington?
No, Freddie Lucian. Oh Freddie Lucian.
Daddy was a good ball player and in them days they had what you call a league club, you know, and this guy picked them up around 25, you ever know anything about 25?
Oh yes, I used to see it, I never got inside though.
Well, them guys used to be around there, you see, and this guy brought him around, this Freddie Lucian brought Jelly Roll more than to our club when we got the piano.
By the way, where was that Orleans club?
Orleans and Pritz, still there. Still there. But I mean it's not no club, no. It's a corner, let's see. It's right straight up this way.
It's on, I mean, is it towards uptown or downtown?
It's just like this corner right here, right there, you know? Across the street? Yeah, across the street on this side, you know, facing the riverside. On the riverside. That's right.
On the riverside and on the downtown.

Yeah, that's it. Take a picture of it that was downtown. Yeah, Orleans Pleasure Club, that was Orleans Pleasure Club. Did you put on parades too? No, I never did on parades. No, no, no, no, just parties. I never tried to make a second line in my life. Really? I never did. I never did. When the parades be coming, the parades be over there, I go over here. I never did like a second line on a parade, I don't know why. But they used to have them. Yes, and when I was in the PWA band, I don't know where they got so many of them. I don't know what to become of the picture. And I'm sitting right on the end, you know what I mean? They can distinguish me, you know, very, you know, because I was bright, a whole lot brighter than the other boys, you see what I mean? By me sitting on the end, I don't know what to become of the picture. And we all, we did, they had over 75 banjo players. And over 40 clarinets. I mean I had never seen a big ban, but we never did play nothing. You know what I mean? So I'm sitting in the band, you know what I mean? I was playing at the Pelican then, when Fate and Marvel and them was playing on the boat, on the steamer captain. And then the lottery closed, and I had to get due, and so the boss man gave me a job playing there. I said, get me a little band. And that's what I got, I got Poinnell. I learned Poinnell how to play piano.
